labels.text: Start the chat in this project

S9.01.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project
S9.01.note: The @ menu lists only open tabs and projects; I found no file or skill picker in the code, and models use the picker in S9.02.
steps: Sign in and open a chat in the side panel.
Click the message box and type @.
Look for the "Projects" heading and the project rows under it, each with "Start the chat in this project".
Type part of a project name after the @ and check that the list narrows to matches.
S9.01.where: Chat composer > type @ > the list under the heading "Projects" (open tabs are listed above it); type part of a project name to narrow the list

S9.02.needs: a signed-in account (without it the menu shows "Sign in for models")
steps: Sign in and open a chat in the side panel.
Click the model button at the top of the chat.
Click "All models" and type part of a model name in "Search models".
Click a model row and check the model button now shows the model you picked.
S9.02.where: Chat, top of the composer > model button showing "AI Assistant" (or the current model name) > "All models (n)" > type in "Search models" > click a model row

S9.06.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project
S9.06.note: A second route exists: the chat title menu has "Add to project". The active project also shows as a chip "Project · NAME" in the header.
steps: Sign in and click the clock icon labelled "Recent chats".
Click "More actions" on a chat row.
Click "Move to project".
Open the list "Project for this chat" and pick a project.
Check the status line "Moved to [project name]." and compare with Expected.
S9.06.where: Recent chats (clock icon in the side panel header) > "More actions" on a chat > "Move to project" > pick a project in the list labelled "Project for this chat"

S9.10.note: No once-versus-always choice was found on this page; the closest is "Allow for this chat" on an approval card (S9.32). The background.ts line in the Code note is a scheduled-task path, not a permission choice.
steps: Click "More" in the side panel header.
Click "Extension settings"; a new tab opens on the Permissions page.
Find "Browser control" and open its menu.
Pick "Ask first" or "Full access" and read the line under the menu.
Compare what is shown with Expected.
S9.10.where: More (button in the side panel header) > "Extension settings" (opens the Permissions page) > "Browser control" menu with Auto, Ask first, Full access, YOLO

S9.12.note: No custom rule option is in the code; the choices are once, daily, weekly and monthly. A chat's title menu "Schedule…" also opens this form.
steps: Click "More" in the side panel header, then "Shortcuts".
In the Schedules section, click "New schedule".
Open "Repeat" and read its choices: Once, Every day, On chosen days of the week, Once a month.
Fill in the form and save; check the new schedule shows its next run time.
S9.12.where: More > "Shortcuts" (opens the Shortcuts page) > "Schedules" section > "New schedule" > "Repeat" menu

S9.19.needs: a request that runs several steps
S9.19.note: Per-step time is shown only on tool steps; the state word appears on a step only when it was cancelled or failed.
steps: Send a request that makes AGI run several steps, such as a browser task.
While it runs, look at the summary line that starts "Working for" above the reply.
Click the summary and read the steps from top to bottom.
Compare the step order and each step's time with Expected.
S9.19.where: Chat, above an assistant reply that ran several steps: the summary line starting "Working for" or "Worked for" (click it to expand the step list)

S9.21.note: I searched apps/extension for board, kanban and column layouts and found none; the only task view is a list sheet opened from "Tasks".

S9.22.needs: a profile where the side panel tour is not done
S9.22.note: The tour has two cards that advance with Next; the code shows no step count and no Back button.
steps: Open the side panel for the first time, on a profile where the tour has not been finished.
Read the card titled "Getting started with AGI" and click "Next".
Read the second card and click "Let's go".
Check whether a step count or a Back button appears, and compare with Expected.
S9.22.where: Side panel on first open (before the tour is finished) > card "Getting started with AGI" > "Next" > "Let's go"

S9.23.note: I searched the onboarding and side panel code for an ordered setup flow; the only setup screen is a welcome page with a sign-in button and a start button, with no name or model step.

S9.28.needs: a question that returns web sources (live web)
S9.28.note: Whether a source appears depends on the answer the assistant gives.
steps: Sign in and ask a question that needs web sources.
Find the source chip in the answer and hover over it (tap it on touch).
Read each source's title, site and excerpt in the card.
Click a source title to open it in a new tab and compare with Expected.
S9.28.where: Chat, an answer that used web sources: the source chip under the answer (shows a site name, or "$SITE$ +$COUNT$" when there are several) > hover or focus it to open the source card

S9.29.note: The row shows only the highest window's percent. The reset time appears in the usage notice when a limit is near or reached, and the screen-reader label is "$PERCENT$% of usage budget used".
steps: Sign in to a paid account; the Usage row is not shown on Free.
Click "More" in the side panel header.
Find the "Usage" row and read its bar and percent.
Compare the percent with Expected; the reset time is not on this row.
S9.29.where: More (button in the side panel header) > "Usage" row with a thin bar and a percent

S9.31.note: I did not find connected-app scopes on this page; the code covers browser sites only.
steps: Click "More" in the side panel header, then "Extension settings".
On the Permissions page, read the "Browser access" text.
Read "Browser control" and its hint about what AGI may do.
Scroll to the approved sites and blocked sites sections and compare with Expected.
S9.31.where: More > "Extension settings" (opens the Permissions page) > "Browser access" text, then "Browser control" and the approved-sites list

labels.text: Your approval is required before this tool can run.

S9.32.needs: a signed-in account and a run that asks for approval
S9.32.note: The ledger had no code location; the card is in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts (appendApprovalActions). "Allow for this chat" is a third choice on the card.
steps: Send a request that makes AGI run a tool step needing approval.
Look for the activity block that opens by itself with the approval message.
Click the step row if its buttons are not visible.
Click "Approve" or "Decline" and check the recorded message and whether the run continues or stops.
S9.32.where: Chat, an activity summary that needs approval (it opens by itself): click the step row that says "Your approval is required before this tool can run." > "Approve" or "Decline"

S9.35.needs: a request that runs a multi-step task
S9.35.note: No separate latest-action field was found; the newest step is the last row when the summary is expanded.
steps: Send a request that makes AGI run a multi-step task.
Watch the summary line "Working for [time]" with its step count.
Wait and check that the time and step count change while it runs.
Click "More" then "Tasks" and check the running task's state.
S9.35.where: Chat, the activity summary above the reply that starts "Working for" and shows the step count; it updates while the run is active

S9.36.needs: a signed-in account and a question that makes AGI show a choice card
S9.36.note: The assistant decides when a card appears; there is no control to request one. Product comparison and itinerary cards are also in interactiveCards.ts.
steps: Sign in and ask a question that leads AGI to offer choices.
In the card, pick one or more answers.
Click "Send answers".
Check that your answers appear as a new message in the chat.
S9.36.where: Chat, a reply that shows a choice card (clarifying question with choices): pick answers in the card > "Send answers"

S9.38.note: The code accepts Command or Ctrl with K; the palette opens only when the side panel has focus.
steps: Click inside the side panel.
Press Command+K.
Type part of a command name or chat title.
Use the arrow keys to move the highlight, then press Enter.
Check the chosen command or chat runs, and that a word with no match shows "No command or chat matches."
S9.38.where: Side panel, with focus inside it: press Command+K > type in "Search commands and chats" > Enter on a result
